title: Commonwealth Startup Fellowship — Cohort 3
funder: Commonwealth Scholarship Commission (CSC) with Imperial College London
amount: Fully funded + up to £2,000 equity-free grant
eligibility: Citizens of low/middle-income Commonwealth countries (Nigeria eligible); business operating 12+ months with commercial traction; graduate-level founder, fluent English
description: Six-month fully funded programme for growth-stage startups: two-week bootcamp in Accra, Ghana (25 Jan–4 Feb 2027, travel/accommodation/visa covered for one founder), five months of 1-on-1 coaching and expert workshops, and a London capstone week (14–21 May 2027) pitching international investors. Teams can apply for up to £2,000 in equity-free grants. Applications close 1 September 2026.

title: SMEDAN Conditional Grant Scheme (₦50,000) — Portal Reopened
deadline: No published deadline — apply early on the official portal
eligibility: Nigerian nano and micro enterprises at Local Government Area level; condition: employ at least one additional person; CAC registration helpful but number requested only if available
description: SMEDAN reopened its Conditional Grant Scheme portal in August 2026. One-time, non-repayable ₦50,000 grant for nano/micro businesses to fund equipment, working capital, technology or expansion, on the condition the business employs at least one additional worker. Apply only through SMEDAN's official portal — the scheme is free; nobody should charge you to apply. Not the same as the Presidential Conditional Grant Scheme.

title: FCMB AgriTech Hackathon & Venture Building Program 2026
funder: FCMB (First City Monument Bank), delivered with Heave Ventures
amount: Cash prizes + venture building support (2026 figures not yet published; 2024 edition awarded ₦23m across top 3 teams)
deadline: Not yet published — applications announced open 31 July 2026
eligibility: Agritech startups/SMEs and developer teams (2024 criteria: registered startups/SMEs in the Agritech sector; confirm 2026 criteria on the application page)
description: Eighth edition of FCMB's agritech competition: a hackathon followed by a venture building programme for agritech founders, historically run with Heave Ventures and FMO. Applications for the 2026 edition announced open on 31 July 2026.

title: Greylight Tangent Cohort 002
amount: Pre-seed cheque plus hands-on build support; Greylight has stated a $1m portfolio deployment target across the programme
eligibility: Early-stage African founders, pre-seed. Cohort 001 companies were mostly Lagos-based technical teams. Confirm current criteria on the application page.
description: Second cohort of Greylight's Tangent programme, a hands-on pre-seed build programme run from Lagos by Managing Partner Joba Adejumo. Cohort 001 concluded with a demo day featuring six startups and faculty including Dr Okechukwu Enelamah.

title: GITEX Nigeria — Startup Festival Exhibitor Call 2026
amount: Subsidised/free startup exhibition space, investor matchmaking and pitch competition access (no direct cash grant)
deadline: Rolling until stands are allocated — event runs 2–3 September 2026
eligibility: Early-stage and growth-stage technology startups. Startup-stage exhibitors apply through the Startup Festival track.
description: Nigeria's first GITEX edition, hosted with NITDA. The Startup Festival track gives startups exhibition space, an investor matchmaking programme and access to the pitch competition. Useful as a route to investors rather than as a cash award.

title: Kjøller — Open Investment Application
eligibility: Open application. Terms and screening criteria are not published; applicants should read the terms on the application page before submitting anything.
description: Open investment application accepted on a rolling basis through the funder's own application page. Amounts and terms are not publicly stated and are assessed case by case.

title: NiYA × Cascador Founders Programme 2026
funder: Nigerian Youth Academy (NiYA) and the Federal Ministry of Youth Development, delivered with Cascador
amount: Up to ₦5,000,000 non-dilutive per founder — awarded to the 8 top performers out of a 20-founder pilot cohort, not to every participant. All 20 also receive NiYA alumni status; winners receive an ERP solution.
deadline: Applications open Wednesday 19 August 2026 on niya.gov.ng — closing date not yet published
eligibility: Early-stage Nigerian founders. Detailed criteria are not yet published; NiYA has said the official requirements will appear on the portal when applications open.
description: Four-week intensive for 20 early-stage Nigerian founders, delivered in person in Abuja with virtual touchpoints. Covers business fundamentals, investment readiness, pitch preparation and one-on-one mentorship. The eight top-performing founders receive up to ₦5m each in non-dilutive funding from Cascador plus an ERP solution. Note that the ₦5m is competitive, not a guaranteed payment to everyone admitted.

title: SMEDAN BRYNE — Building Resilient Young Nigerian Entrepreneurs
funder: Small and Medium Enterprises Development Agency of Nigeria (SMEDAN)
amount: ₦250,000 seed funding to each of 52 weekly startup hackathon winners per year. The incubation, campus and digital tracks provide training, mentorship and market access rather than cash.
deadline: Not yet published — programme launched 14 August 2026; application routes for each track had not been announced at the time of listing
eligibility: Young Nigerians at various stages: students at tertiary institutions (campus track), and young entrepreneurs nationwide in sectors including fashion, woodwork and agriculture (incubation track).
description: SMEDAN's youth entrepreneurship project, launched on International Youth Day 2026 by Director-General Charles Odii, targeting more than 100,000 young Nigerians a year across four tracks: an incubation programme for 600 entrepreneurs annually through the Industrial Development Centres; a Campus Enterprise Engagement Platform run with the Federal Ministry of Education reaching up to 3,000 students per campus; BRYNE Digital Connect for online entrepreneurship education and market linkage; and a weekly startup hackathon targeting 5,000 entrepreneurs, of whom 52 winners receive ₦250,000 seed funding each.
status_note: unveiled 14 Aug 2026; no eligibility document or application window published yet

title: Pan-African timbuktoo Launchpad for HealthTech Startups
funder: UNDP timbuktoo HealthTech Hub, Kigali, Rwanda
amount: No direct cash award. Structured incubation through accredited Entrepreneurship Support Organisations, mentorship, the Seedstars SIGMA platform, investment-readiness support, demo days, and stated pathways to acceleration programmes and early-stage investment.
deadline: Rolling, by quarterly cohort. Cohort 1 (September 2026) is CLOSED. Cohort 2 (December 2026) date not yet announced — the application form stays open between cohorts.
eligibility: HealthTech startups based in Africa or targeting African healthcare markets. Must have a working prototype or MVP, a committed founding team, a clearly defined healthcare problem, and demonstrable scalability. Open from anywhere in Africa, including countries with no accredited incubator yet.
description: UNDP's pan-African HealthTech incubation programme, run from the timbuktoo HealthTech Hub in Kigali and delivered through a network of accredited incubators, roughly five startups each. Runs up to 12 months per cohort, opening with a three-month core curriculum. Note this is a capacity and network programme, not a grant — no cash award is attached, though it routes into acceleration and investment pathways.
